title: AI Cat Dance
summary: Make an AI cat dance video from one photo of your cat: the cat dance effect, the exact prompts behind it and eight example clips. Free to try in Flick.
body_markdown:
### How do I make my cat dance with AI?


Upload a photo of your cat with its whole body in frame as the start frame of an image to video model, describe a few dance moves such as standing up, swaying and waving its paws, keep the camera still and generate a short clip.


### Is there a free AI cat dance generator?


Yes. Flick is free to start: the free plan gives 100 credits every day with no credit card, enough to animate a photo of your cat into a short dancing clip.


### What kind of cat photo works best for an AI cat dance?


A sharp, well lit photo of the cat facing the camera with its whole body visible from ears to tail and some empty space around it works best, because the model needs room to move the paws, body and tail.


### Can a cat that is lying down or sitting do the AI cat dance?


Yes. Ask a sitting cat to sit up tall and wave its front paws or sway its body, and ask a cat on all fours to rise onto its hind legs first, so the moves fit the pose in the photo.


### How do I keep my cat looking the same in an AI dance video?


Keep the moves simple, keep the camera still, and end the prompt with same cat, same place, then generate again if its fur pattern, eye colour or markings change during the dance.


### Can I add music to an AI cat dance video?


Yes. Make the clip first, then add a song when you post it, or generate a music track in Flick to go with it, and line the paw waves up with the beat of the music.


### Can I make two cats or a cat and a dog dance together?


Yes. Start from one photo with both animals fully in frame and side by side, then describe each one's moves in the prompt, such as the cat waving its paws while the dog bounces, and keep the camera still.
